bridge_guide.text: Telford's bridge hangs on sixteen wrought iron chains. They are held at each end in tunnels cut into the rock.
Before the bridge, you crossed by ferry, or you swam, or you waited for a tide, or you did not cross. Quite the commute.

island_farmer.text: Anglesey's sheep and cattle are grand, but our sea salt is famous. Halen Môn, they call it.
Roman soldiers wrote that the druids made their last stand on this island. It's got a lot of history for a place that mostly has fields.

stone_student.text: Bryn Celli Ddu is the passage tomb. The sun comes through the gap on the summer solstice. It's like a timer for the dead.
I'm a volunteer. My job is to stand here and stop people climbing on the stones. And to look cross about it, which I do very well.

sign_reader.text: I've been trying to read the long sign for twenty minutes. I've got as far as 'Llan'.
Locals call the place Llanfair PG. The ticket office sells you the short name. Cheeky.

strait_sailor.text: That's the Menai Strait. It's got fierce tides and a beautiful temper.
The tide runs one way through the strait for six hours, then the other way. Dread to think what the fish make of it.
